text:
maria: Quick heads-up — the PR that wires smart routing + fallback to the quantized v-small model is ready but blocked on architecture sign-off. RFC here: https://rfc.redwood.company/r/354-routing-fallback (updated). PR here: https://git.redwood/company/redwood-inference/pull/8123. Summary: changes to request routing policy + adds an automated fallback path when high latency or memory pressure is observed. This is intentionally gated on the RFC because it affects request-level routing and SLOs.

aj: I can review later today. Quick Q: does this change require any DB/schema migrations or product coordination?

maria: No DB/schema migrations — it's purely runtime routing and config. No product migration needed. I've added a short canary plan below and a smoke test in ci/canary.sh.

samir: I left a comment on the RFC (section 3.2) about KV cache TTL and cold-start behavior. Design looks fine overall, but want to see a short note about fallback latency budget (how long we attempt model X before switching).

maria: Good call — updated RFC to add a 100ms budget per fallback attempt and a max cumulative 400ms before switching to the smaller variant. Pushed a follow-up commit to both the RFC and the PR.

tess: If arch signs off, who will actually run the canary and monitor metrics?

maria: I'll kick off the canary and monitor. Plan below. Will ping eng-oncall if anything anomalous shows up and will promote to canary stage owner if someone else wants it.

CANARY PLAN (short):
- Stages: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% traffic over ~4 hours (30–60m windows).
- Metrics to watch: p50/p95 latency, p99 tail, 5xx error rate, model-mismatch rate (unexpected token diff), request drop/retry rate.
- Fail conditions: +20% p95 vs baseline OR p99 > 2s OR 5xx > 0.5% sustained for 5 min -> rollback.
- Safety: automatic fallback to non-quantized variant on memory-pressure events. Canary run will be isolated to a dedicated pool.
- Smoke tests: ci/canary.sh (integration + simple prompt set) run prior to 1% rollout.

Note: The repo PR is labeled `rfc-gated` and the merge pipeline will block until RFC status = accepted. deploy-bot: please keep the gating in place.

deploy-bot: PR 8123 marked rfc-gated. Merge blocked until RFC 354 state=accepted.

aj: :thumbsup: I'll do a focused review tomorrow morning and follow up on the small comments. If samir + aj give arch ack we can merge once RFC is accepted.

samir: I can give arch ack after the TTL sentence is in the RFC and I verify the smoke test covers a cold-cache case.

maria: Thanks — I've added a cold-cache test case to ci/canary.sh and documented the rollback playbook in the RFC appendix. Ping me if you want me to walk through the canary dashboard live. :handshake:
